newsitem.title: USA: MSRB proposes tighter deadlines for sending OS.
newsitem.headline: MSRB proposes tighter deadlines for sending OS.

text.p: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board proposed tightening the deadline by which bond dealers must get final official statements to customers in primary offerings, an advance copy of the board's quarterly report to dealers says.
Comments are due by November 15 on this and other proposed amendments to the board's rule G-32, which sets disclosure standards for new issues of municipal bonds.

The draft amendment would move up the time that a customer receives a final official statement from the date of settlement to the date the final money confirmation is sent by the dealer to the customer.
Delivery, in no event, could occur later than the date of settlement, under the proposed amendment to rule G-32, according to MSRB's five-page notice.
The notice asks for comments on whether final OSs are received in sufficent time to comply with such a proposal.
"Would the draft amendment effectively ensure that customers receive official satements before paying for securities?" MSRB asks.
MSRB also wants to know whether the rule should address alternative ways of sending official statements to customers.
Should MSRB require dealers to send OSs in ways that ensures customers will get them, such as first class mail or overnight delivery, the notice asks.
The draft amendment also would require the managing underwriter to provide, upon request, a copy of the official statement to purchasing dealers.

It also would require the managing underwriter to provide one additional copy of the OS per $100,000 par value to purchasing dealers who purchase for resale to customers, as well as instructions on how to order copies of the OS from the printer.
"How are dealers that are not in the underwriting group currently obtaining official statements?" MSRB asks.
"Are sufficient quantities of official statements available in a timely manner?"
